tells.1: Filler opener “We wanted to let you know” and stiff “at which time” legalese that clashes with the casual close.
tells.2: Brochure-smooth cadence, especially “will take effect for you” and the padded “to give you more options during the week.”
tells.3: Stacked casual pivots: “Quick heads-up,” “On a happier note,” and “we’ll be glad to help.”
tells.5: Stock benefit add-on: “so you’ll have more options during the week.”

reason: Versions 4 and 5 read most like a skilled person writing a price notice: direct, unpadded, and free of performed cheer. I’d send 5 — the grandfathered rate is unambiguous, the tone is natural, and it stays warm without version 3’s spin.
